project.name: Sawtry

properties.name: Sawtry curated visitor boundary
properties.methodology: Morphological closing of the existing curated visitor boundary using a 150 metre outward and inward buffer. This preserves its deliberate visitor extensions while filling internal omissions for connected parks, river corridors and visitor green spaces.

project.boundarySource: Curated Sawtry visitor boundary: the original ONS 2024 built-up area plus a narrow extension to the directly adjoining St Judith’s Field and CARESCO community cluster.
project.researchNotes: Full visitor audit completed 2026-08-08. Bundled Historic England data was filtered against the unchanged ONS locality. Public planner points use a transparent narrow visitor extension for St Judith’s Field and CARESCO. Sawtry Abbey, the medieval moat, Aversley Wood, Archers Wood, Old St Andrew’s churchyard, private/customer parking and dinner-only venues were excluded. No exact Sawtry match was found in the reviewed Treasure Trails catalogue. Historic England official list-entry date enrichment completed 2026-08-08: 12 of 13 statutory records now carry defensible date evidence; unresolved entries were individually checked and retained as unknown. Standalone attraction audit added 2026-08-08. These regional destinations are outside the active town boundary, appear only on Home discovery, and do not alter the town tourist rating.

touristAppeal.label: Not a tourist town
touristAppeal.summary: Sawtry has genuine local interest in All Saints, the Green and lock-up, but the visitor offer is small, lightly interpreted and has limited daytime food and facilities. The medieval moat, nearby woods and abbey remains lie beyond the town boundary and do not raise its rating.

townGuide.headline: A quiet village green, a tiny lock-up and the story of three old parishes
townGuide.intro: Sawtry is a local-history pause rather than a tourist destination. Link the Green and its two-cell lock-up with All Saints, then use St Judith’s Field for a picnic or family break. The medieval moat is outside the strict town polygon and is not counted in this guide.
perfectFor: An hour or two while passing nearby
Visitors interested in overlooked village history

suggestedFirstVisit.title: The Green, the lock-up and All Saints
suggestedFirstVisit.summary: Begin at the Green and lock-up, walk north to All Saints, then return to St Judith’s Field if you need play space or picnic tables.

dontMiss: All Saints Church and war memorial
The Green and historic village lock-up
townGuide.visitorMood: Best approached as a quiet local-history stop, with modest facilities and no major visitor attraction.

visitorHighlights.name: All Saints Church and war memorial
visitorHighlights.reason: Visit Sawtry’s Victorian parish church, rebuilt in 1880 with stone from the village’s older churches, and use its churchyard setting to connect the three historic parishes.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Interior opening varies; exterior and memorial are visible from public approaches.

attractionGuide.headline: One church carrying the memory of three old Sawtry parishes
attractionGuide.intro: All Saints is modest but historically revealing: its Victorian rebuilding reused stone from the village’s lost churches and preserves the memory of an older three-parish settlement.
attractionGuide.toilets: No general visitor toilet is advertised at the church.

thingsToDo.name: Read the setting against Sawtry’s three-parish story

visitorHighlights.name: The Green and historic village lock-up
visitorHighlights.reason: Pause on the village green beside Sawtry’s small Grade II lock-up, a two-cell reminder of local policing and weekend misbehaviour in the old village.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Outdoor public green; lock-up interior is not regularly advertised as open.

attractionGuide.headline: A tiny lock-up with a memorable village story
attractionGuide.intro: Sawtry’s Green is a simple orientation point, but the surviving two-cell lock-up gives it a distinctive historical detail and an easy story to remember.

thingsToDo.name: Inspect its small two-cell form from outside

visitorHighlights.reason: Use Sawtry’s main recreation ground for a family pause, play equipment, picnic tables and open space at the village edge.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Public outdoor recreation ground; best in daylight.

attractionGuide.headline: Sawtry’s useful family and picnic pause
attractionGuide.intro: St Judith’s Field is practical rather than destination-scale, offering play, picnic tables and open space for visitors already passing through the village.
attractionGuide.picnic: Public picnic tables are provided at St Judith’s Field.

attractionGuide.headline: Silver-birch woodland, deep peat and one of Britain's lowest landscapes
attractionGuide.intro: Holme Fen feels unlike a conventional woodland. The peat, birches and enormous skies tell the story of a drained landscape slowly being reconnected through the Great Fen.

attractionGuide.heroAlt: Ink-and-watercolour illustration of a reflective fen drain between tall reedbeds at Woodwalton Fen
attractionGuide.headline: A rare surviving fen of reedbeds, pools, hides and extraordinary wildlife
attractionGuide.intro: Woodwalton is the more serious nature reserve of the Great Fen pair. Its history, habitats and three trails are exceptional, but water levels and strict no-dog rules need planning.
attractionGuide.toilets: No public toilets are provided at the reserve.
